headings.text: How to Recognize a Stroke: Act F.A.S.T.

widgets.text: A stroke is a critical medical emergency that cuts off blood flow to the brain. Recognizing the warning signs early can save a life. The CDC recommends the F.A.S.T. method to identify a stroke:Face Drooping: Does one side of the face droop or feel completely numb?Arm Weakness: Ask the person to raise both arms. Does one arm drift downward?Speech Difficulty: Is their speech suddenly slurred or impossible to understand?Time to Call 911: If you observe any of these signs, seek emergency stroke care immediately.Mini strokes, clinically known as transient ischemic attacks (TIAs), produce similar symptoms and are a massive warning sign of a future stroke. Risk factors like high blood pressure, diabetes, and smoking drastically increase your chances of a neurological event. Do not ignore these symptoms.Our stroke evaluation at ER of White Rock includes immediate diagnostic imaging, vital sign stabilization, and coordination of thrombolytic therapies for ischemic and hemorrhagic strokes.Stroke recognition is one piece of broader cardiovascular awareness. Our cardiovascular emergencies guide near White Rock covers heart attack, stroke, and blood clot warning signs.

headings.text: Why Choose ER of White Rock for Stroke Emergencies?

widgets.text: Understanding Your Stroke Risk Factors

While our East Dallas facility is here to provide life-saving care, understanding stroke prevention is just as important for protecting your family. The NIH NINDS identifies high blood pressure as the leading cause of strokes and brain bleeds. If you or a loved one have a history of hypertension, taking proactive steps is vital:Manage Blood Pressure: Check your levels regularly and take all prescribed medications.Control Diabetes: High blood sugar damages blood vessels over time and increases clot risks.Quit Smoking: Smoking thickens your blood and drastically increases the chance of plaque buildup.Watch for Warning Signs: Sudden dizziness, severe unexplained headaches, or temporary vision loss are warning signs that require an immediate ER evaluation.

headings.text: What to Do If You Suspect a Brain Bleed or Stroke

widgets.text: If you or a family member show signs of a stroke, take these exact steps to ensure the best possible medical outcome:Note the Exact Time: Look at the clock the moment symptoms begin. This critical detail dictates which medications our doctors can safely use.Keep the Patient Awake: Do not let them go to sleep to see if the symptoms pass. Keep them alert.Do Not Give Aspirin or Food: If they are having a brain bleed, blood thinners like aspirin can be fatal. If their throat muscles are affected, food or water can cause choking.Act Immediately: Call 911 or drive directly to our Dallas emergency room.
Get Immediate Care Now
